slides.title: Thought Leadership Needs a Deliberate Strategy
bullets: Being recognized as a thought leader takes a sustained content strategy, not occasional posts
The goal is a recognizable presence built over time
It always stays within scientific rigor and non-promotion limits

slides.title: Define a Precise Area of Focus
bullets: Pick a specific area to be known for: a therapeutic area, AI in Medical Affairs, insight excellence
Trying to cover everything dispersedly dilutes recognition
A clear focus helps the audience associate you with that topic

slides.title: Consistency Beats Sporadic Bursts
bullets: Regular activity, even at moderate frequency, builds visibility far more effectively
Content doesn't have to be fully original
Commenting substantively on relevant publications or summarizing a congress finding works just as well

slides.title: Format for the Platform
bullets: Short, visually clear, directly useful content drives more genuine interaction
Lengthy or overly technical text tends to underperform
A short video or infographic can show both scientific knowledge and communication skill

slides.title: Compliance Comes Before Every Post
bullets: Follow internal digital communication policies before publishing anything
Avoid any appearance of product promotion
Keep personal scientific opinion clearly separate from official company positioning
Verify sources with the same rigor as any scientific communication

slides.title: A Tool That Opens Doors
bullets: Thought leadership is not an end in itself, it amplifies personal brand
Done well and sustained, it opens new collaborations and relevant invitations
It builds visibility with hiring decision-makers long before you look for a new role

takeaway.title: LinkedIn thought leadership amplifies personal brand when built with focus and consistency
bullets: A precise area of focus makes recognition possible
Consistency, even moderate, beats sporadic original content
Compliance and format discipline protect credibility while building visibility
